A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same QSHNN research despite the revised title. Their text, equations, figures and appendices support comparison; v3 retains Appendices A–G and adds Appendix H.

before.justification: Section 4 and Figures 5–7 report original training and dynamical-system experiments on generated quaternion targets. Figure 8 reports a preliminary PyBullet robotic simulation.

after.justification: v3 retains the original training, weight-pattern and trajectory results in Figures 5–7 and the preliminary robotic simulation in Figure 8.

M1.justification: The dynamics, learning objectives, gradient updates and periodic Frobenius projection in Section 3 and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The corrected background matrices and Appendix H do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate generated quaternion targets and retain the same preliminary PyBullet scenario. PandaReach, FetchReach and random workspace alignment in Appendix E remain proposed future benchmarks.

E2.justification: SHNN remains the empirical comparator in Figures 5–6. Appendix F retains the same prospective IK, CHOMP, STOMP and RRT-Connect plus smoothing baselines without adding reported comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains the four-neuron setup, uniform target generation, 10^-6 error thresholds and iteration caps of 30,000 for QSHNN and 10,000 for SHNN. Algorithm 1 and the evaluation procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: The projection/no-projection comparison, alternate initialization and target-symmetry cases in Figure 6, and robotic demonstration remain unchanged. No additional ablation, robustness test or empirical case study appears.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same statistical reporting practice, with no added run or seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Figures 5–8 contain identical training curves, weight heat maps, state trajectories and robotic demonstration images. Their associated empirical findings are unchanged, with no added or removed result entries.

T1.justification: Appendix H substantially expands the formal background with nonzero-quaternion Lie groups, representation and orthogonality identities, rotation-group correspondences and Lie-bracket relations. v3 also corrects the basis matrices from v2 Eq. (2.2) in Eq. (2.3). The existing stability, projection, curvature and error-decay proofs otherwise retain their mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: supervised quaternion Hopfield dynamics, stability guarantees, periodic structure-preserving projection and smooth trajectories. The revised title does not establish a different core contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix H adds explanations of the skew-symmetric coupling and rotational interpretation without a unit-norm constraint. It newly interprets the existing projection algorithm as manifold optimization and a first-order approximation to Riemannian gradient descent. Section 5's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The Python implementation, Apple M1 hardware, memory, Runge–Kutta solver and disclosed hyperparameters remain unchanged. No new code/data access information or reproducibility instructions are supplied.

R1.justification: v3 adds algebra and Lie-theory references by Grillet, Hall and Voight to support Appendix H. The positioning against earlier quaternion and Hopfield networks remains unchanged; the added conference self-reference identifies the same research work.

P1.justification: v3 revises the title, author/contact footnotes and publication note, adds Appendix H and its cross-reference, and expands Appendix G's heading. Other prose receives limited edits, with the main narrative and section order preserved.

P2.justification: The basis-matrix display is reformatted, opening and reference text reflows, and several appendix derivations receive separately numbered lines. Figures 1–8 retain their images and placement; no figures or tables are added.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects the main-text basis matrices and adds useful geometric context. However, new Eq. (H.3) gives basis entries incompatible with corrected Eq. (2.3), while Appendix H's nonzero-quaternion group distinction remains unreconciled with Section 2's all-quaternion group claim. These competing effects on mathematical clarity leave the net quality benefit uncertain.
